### T1543.003: AuKill EDR Killer Abusing Signed Sysinternals PROCEXP152.SYS (BYOVD)
- **ID:** `aukill-edr-killer-procxp152-byovd`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/aukill-edr-killer-procxp152-byovd
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=aukill-edr-killer-procxp152-byovd
- **Category:** KERNEL_FIRMWARE_BYOVD | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a building where normal workers are forbidden from touching the security cameras (Protected Process Light). However, an old master maintenance robot built by the building’s own manufacturer (Sysinternals PROCEXP152.SYS) has a valid master badge and will obey anyone who pushes its buttons (IOCTL 0x8335003C). A burglar wheels the old maintenance robot out of a backpack and orders it to unplug every security camera in the building. Dissected by Sophos X-Ops and Elastic Security Labs in 2023 across Medusa Locker and LockBit intrusions, AuKill is a C++ Bring Your Own Vulnerable Driver (BYOVD) tool. It drops version 16.32 of Microsoft’s signed Sysinternals Process Explorer kernel driver (PROCEXP152.SYS) into System32\drivers and issues DeviceIoControl codes 0x8335003C (open protected process handle) and 0x83350004 (close handle) to strip handles and kill PPL-protected EDR/AV services from Ring 0.
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Dropping & Registering Vulnerable Signed PROCEXP152.SYS v16.32 (T1543.003) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Opening \\.\PROCEXP152 & Issuing IOCTL 0x8335003C / 0x83350004 (T1562.001) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Ring-0 Termination of PPL EDR Sensors & Ransomware Detonation (T1486)
- **Primary Sources:** [Microsoft Win32 API Reference: CreateProcessW (CREATE_SUSPENDED), VirtualAllocEx & WriteProcessMemory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw); [Microsoft Sysinternals: Sysmon Event ID 25: ProcessTampering (Image is replaced)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-25-processtampering); [Elastic Security Labs: Hunting Memory Injection & Process Tampering via Kernel ETW Threat Intelligence](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs)

### T1553.002: STONESTOP & POORTRY / BURNTCIGAR WHQL-Signed Kernel Callback Wiper

- **Overview:** Instead of tricking an old maintenance robot, a syndicate sets up a fake hardware company, submits their own custom-built assassin robot to the official city licensing office (WHQL Attestation Signing), gets an official holographic seal stamped onto it, and walks it right into the central nervous system of the building where it erases the phone numbers of every security guard on the emergency call list (PspCreateProcessNotifyRoutine). Unmasked by PwC Threat Intelligence (attributing it to China-nexus APT Red Menshen) and analyzed in depth by Sandfly Security and Elastic, BPFDoor is a passive Linux/Solaris implant that evaded detection for over five years across telecom and government networks. ### T1542.001: CosmicStrand Motherboard SPI Flash UEFI Rootkit (CSMCORE -> ntoskrnl.exe Chain)

- **Overview:** Imagine a ghost etched directly into the silicon blueprint of a building’s foundation (SPI Flash Chip). Even if the owner bulldozes the interior walls and installs a brand-new hard drive and operating system, the moment the main power breaker is flipped on, the ghost whispers to the foundation controller (CSMCORE), who whispers to the elevator operator (bootmgfw.efi), who whispers to the floor manager (winload.efi), who finally slips a mind-control chip into the building director (ntoskrnl.exe) before the director even opens their eyes. Detailed by Kaspersky GReAT in July 2022, CosmicStrand is an advanced China-nexus UEFI firmware rootkit residing inside the physical SPI NOR flash chip of ASUS and Gigabyte H81 motherboards. Because it lives in motherboard firmware rather than on the hard drive, it survives full disk formatting and drive replacement. On every boot, its patched CSMCORE DXE driver hooks HandleProtocol to propagate a fileless in-memory hook chain through bootmgfw.efi and winload.efi directly into ntoskrnl.exe, disabling Kernel Patch Protection (PatchGuard) and deploying a Ring-0 implant.

Jointly disclosed by BlackBerry and Intezer in June 2022 targeting Latin American financial institutions, Symbiote is a userland Linux rootkit compiled as a shared object (.so) library rather than a standalone executable. - **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=hermeticwiper-ukraine-easeus-mbr-wipe
- **Category:** RANSOMWARE_EXTORTION | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a saboteur disguised with a genuine business license (Hermetica Digital Ltd) who wants to demolish a library’s card catalog ($MFT) and front entrance (MBR) so not a single book can ever be found again. Because the library’s operating system guards the master card catalog, the saboteur unpacks a genuine, licensed bulldozer (Signed EaseUS Partition Master Driver empntdrv.sys) from their suitcase, drives it straight into the foundation, shreds the master index with random noise, and pulls the main power plug. Discovered by ESET and analyzed by SentinelOne and CISA (AA22-057A / MAR-10375867-1) on February 23, 2022, HermeticWiper (FoxBlade) is a destructive wiper deployed by Russia’s GRU Sandworm group against Ukrainian ministries and financial institutions. Signed with a code-signing certificate issued to Hermetica Digital Ltd, the binary carries compressed 32/64-bit copies of the legitimate, Microsoft-signed EaseUS Partition Master kernel driver (empntdrv.sys) in its RCDATA resource section. It loads the driver, disables Volume Shadow Copies and crash dumps, and uses CryptGenRandom to overwrite the Master Boot Record (MBR), partition tables, and NTFS metadata ($MFT, $LogFile, $Bitmap) across \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 before forcing a reboot.
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Extracting & Registering Signed EaseUS Driver (empntdrv.sys) from RCDATA (T1068) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Disabling Volume Shadow Copy (vss), Crash Dumps & Fragmenting NTFS Metadata (T1490) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Raw \\.\PhysicalDrive0..100 MBR & NTFS $MFT Overwrite with CSPRNG Bytes (T1561.002)
- **Primary Sources:** [Microsoft Win32 API Reference: CreateProcessW (CREATE_SUSPENDED), VirtualAllocEx & WriteProcessMemory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw); [Microsoft Sysinternals: Sysmon Event ID 25: ProcessTampering (Image is replaced)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-25-processtampering); [Elastic Security Labs: Hunting Memory Injection & Process Tampering via Kernel ETW Threat Intelligence](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs)

### T1199: AcidRain MIPS ELF Satellite Modem Wiper (/dev/mtd MEMERASE / Viasat KA-SAT)
- **ID:** `acidrain-viasat-ka-sat-modem-wiper`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/acidrain-viasat-ka-sat-modem-wiper
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=acidrain-viasat-ka-sat-modem-wiper
- **Category:** RANSOMWARE_EXTORTION | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine 40,000 remote satellite dishes across Europe that all listen to a single central control tower (TR-069 ACS) for automatic software updates. Saboteurs break into the control tower and broadcast a tiny self-destruct program (AcidRain / ukrop) that tells every satellite modem not just to delete its files, but to use a blowtorch (MEMERASE / MEMWRITEOOB IOCTLs) to melt the permanent flash memory chip (/dev/mtd*) holding its startup brain, turning the hardware into a dead brick. Reverse-engineered by SentinelOne (SentinelLabs) in March 2022 and addressed in joint CISA/NSA/FBI SATCOM advisories, AcidRain (ukrop) is a 32-bit big-endian MIPS ELF wiper deployed by Russian GRU threat actors against Viasat’s KA-SAT network on February 24, 2022. Pushed over the legitimate TR-069 CWMP management channel to over 40,000 SurfBeam2 satellite modems (knocking out Ukrainian communications and 5,800 German wind turbines), AcidRain exhaustively iterates Linux block devices (/dev/sd*, /dev/mmcblk*) and raw Memory Technology Devices (/dev/mtd0..99), issuing MEMUNLOCK, MEMERASE, and MEMWRITEOOB IOCTLs to permanently erase the onboard SPI NOR/NAND flash.
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Management Plane Compromise & TR-069 CWMP Push of MIPS ELF Binary (ukrop) (T1199) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Block Device Enumeration (/dev/sda, /dev/mmcblk) & Sequential Overwrite (T1561.002) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Raw SPI Flash /dev/mtd0..99 Destruction via MEMUNLOCK, MEMERASE & MEMWRITEOOB (T1495)
- **Primary Sources:** [Microsoft Win32 API Reference: CreateProcessW (CREATE_SUSPENDED), VirtualAllocEx & WriteProcessMemory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw); [Microsoft Sysinternals: Sysmon Event ID 25: ProcessTampering (Image is replaced)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-25-processtampering); [Elastic Security Labs: Hunting Memory Injection & Process Tampering via Kernel ETW Threat Intelligence](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs)

### T1053.005: Sandworm ArguePatch Loader & CaddyWiper Domain-Aware Disk Wiper (T1561.001)
- **ID:** `caddywiper-arguepatch-gpo-destruction`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/caddywiper-arguepatch-gpo-destruction
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=caddywiper-arguepatch-gpo-destruction
- **Category:** RANSOMWARE_EXTORTION | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine an army of demolition robots dispatched from a central radio tower (Primary Domain Controller) to tear down every building in a compound. If the first robot to wake up accidentally demolishes the central radio tower itself, none of the remaining buildings will ever receive the demolition signal! So the robot’s first instruction (DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation) is: "Check if I am standing inside the central radio tower. If yes, go to sleep immediately; if no, erase every room and smash the foundation." Analyzed by ESET, Cisco Talos, and CERT-UA in March–April 2022 during Sandworm attacks against Ukrainian financial and energy organizations (including alongside Industroyer2), CaddyWiper is a compact 9KB C++ destructive wiper often loaded in memory by ArguePatch (a patched version of Hex-Rays IDA Pro’s signed/legitimate win32_remote.exe debugger server). Pushed via Active Directory GPO Scheduled Tasks, CaddyWiper first calls DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation and exits immediately if running on a Primary Domain Controller (DsRole_RolePrimaryDomainController), then recursively zeroes out C:\Users and drives D:..Z: before wiping disk partition tables on \\.\PhysicalDrive9..0 via IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX (0x0007C054).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: GPO Mass Deployment & ArguePatch Patched Debugger Loader Execution (T1053.005) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: DsRoleGetPrimaryDomainInformation Check to Spare Domain Controllers (T1082) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: TakeOwnership Recursive File Zeroing & IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX Wipe (T1561.001)
- **Primary Sources:** [Microsoft Win32 API Reference: CreateProcessW (CREATE_SUSPENDED), VirtualAllocEx & WriteProcessMemory](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw); [Microsoft Sysinternals: Sysmon Event ID 25: ProcessTampering (Image is replaced)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-25-processtampering); [Elastic Security Labs: Hunting Memory Injection & Process Tampering via Kernel ETW Threat Intelligence](https://www.elastic.co/security-labs)

### T1190: VulnCheck — Control Web Panel (CWP) Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE (CVE-2026-73695..104080)
- **ID:** `vulncheck-cwp-preauth-module-dispatch-rce`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/vulncheck-cwp-preauth-module-dispatch-rce
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=vulncheck-cwp-preauth-module-dispatch-rce
- **Category:** ZERO_DAY_APPLIANCES | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a multi-tenant apartment building (Control Web Panel port 2083) where the front-desk guard (CWPUserIndex::__construct) tells unauthenticated visitors "Please go to the lobby login desk" (emitting an HTTP 302 Location header, CVE-2026-73696) but forgets to actually lock the inner hallway door (omitting exit()). The visitor walks straight past the desk into any tenant suite (include_once modules/$module.php, CVE-2026-73695), uses the suite maintenance panel (phpini_editor.php, CVE-2026-73697) to run commands as that tenant, and then picks up the building internal house phone (loopback API 127.0.0.1:2302, CVE-2026-77877 & CVE-2026-77878) which executes every request as the building master superintendent (root uid=0). Disclosed by VulnCheck in November 2026 ("Control Web Panel: Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE"), this 10-CVE chain compromises Control Web Panel (CWP) instances in two network hops. First, an unauthenticated attacker enumerates a valid hosting username via an HTTP 302 vs 404 oracle on port 2083 and exploits an Execution After Redirect (EAR) flaw in UnauthenticatedFlowTrait::toLoginWithIntendedUri() (CVE-2026-73696) combined with unvalidated module LFI in services/users/index.php (CVE-2026-73695) to reach any of the 170+ user modules without a session. Second, the attacker triggers pre-auth file write or command injection in modules/phpini_editor.php (CVE-2026-73697) or modules/protected_directory.php (CVE-2026-77876) as the hosting user, and immediately relays a loopback request to the root-privileged Slim v2 User API on 127.0.0.1:2302 (/v1/restoredatabase/ CVE-2026-77877 & CVE-2026-77878, /valid_token/ CVE-2026-104080, or OAuth SQLi CVE-2026-77879 + /v1/newpass/ CVE-2026-77880) to achieve unauthenticated root RCE.
- **Stages (4):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Account Enumeration Oracle, Execution After Redirect (CVE-2026-73696) & Module LFI (CVE-2026-73695) (T1190) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Pre-Auth Hosting Account RCE via phpini_editor.php (CVE-2026-73697) & protected_directory.php (CVE-2026-77876) (T1059.004) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Single-Request Root Escalation via Loopback User API 127.0.0.1:2302 (CVE-2026-77877, CVE-2026-77878 & CVE-2026-104080) (T1068) -> Stage 4: Stage 4: Loopback OAuth SQLi Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-77879), /v1/newpass/ Root RCE (CVE-2026-77880) & Blind SQLi (CVE-2026-77881) (T1552.001)
- **Primary Sources:** [VulnCheck Initial Access Intelligence (CNA): Control Web Panel: Pre-Auth Module Dispatch to Root RCE (CVE-2026-73695..CVE-2026-104080)](https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/control-web-panel-pre-auth-module-dispatch-rce); [Control Web Panel (CentOS Web Panel): CWP7 ChangeLog & Security Updates (Builds 0.9.8.1210 to 0.9.8.1213+ / Patches 1.12–1.30)](https://control-webpanel.com/changelog); [NIST NVD & CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV): Control Web Panel Historical Pre-Auth RCE Context (CVE-2025-48703 & CWE-698 Execution After Redirect)](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-48703)

### T1003.003: CISA & Microsoft DFIR — Volume Shadow Copy & esentutl.exe NTDS.dit Extraction Forensics
- **ID:** `dfir-ntds-dit-vssadmin-esentutl-extraction`

- **Category:** ACTIVE_DIRECTORY | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a high-security bank vault where the master ledger book (ntds.dit) is bolted to the teller desk while the bank is open, so an insider uses the building photocopy system (Volume Shadow Copy vssvc.exe) to photograph the entire room and uses the official ledger binding machine (esentutl.exe) to print a duplicate copy alongside the safe combination key (SYSTEM registry hive). Grounded in CISA Advisory AA23-075A, Microsoft ESENT Event Logging documentation, and MITRE ATT&CK T1003.003: an adversary with Domain Admin privileges creates a Volume Shadow Copy of C: on a Domain Controller via vssadmin.exe or ntdsutil.exe, copies the locked Active Directory database (C:\Windows\NTDS\ntds.dit) using esentutl.exe /y /vss, and extracts the SYSTEM registry hive for offline password hash cracking. Across this 3-step forensic reconstruction, incident responders correlate primary host, kernel, identity, and network telemetry (capturing exact Event IDs, syscall numbers, registry/filesystem structures, and protocol fields so defenders can verify root cause and scope compromise with high confidence).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Volume Shadow Copy Creation via vssadmin.exe & vssvc.exe (EventID 1 & 7036) (T1003.003) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: ESENT Database Streaming via esentutl.exe /y /vss (Application ESENT EventID 325 & 326) (T1003.003) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: SYSTEM Registry Hive BootKey Extraction (reg.exe save HKLM\SYSTEM) & Offline SecretsDump (T1003.002)

- **Overview:** Imagine a high-security facility where an intruder attempts to operate covertly across Attacker C2 (wss://castleservices.org), NPM & Unpinned CDN (unpkg / jsDelivr @latest), and Production Web App (@lottiefiles/lottie-player@2.0.7), unaware that every system call, protocol handshake, and on-disk structural table (End-User Browser DOM & Web3 Wallet (AceDrainer)) automatically records an immutable forensic ledger entry correlated by CSP / Subresource Integrity (SRI) Browser Sensor. Grounded in the official LottieFiles incident post-mortem, Snyk Security Labs, and Wiz Research: attackers compromise a developer’s NPM access token to publish malicious versions 2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7 of the popular @lottiefiles/lottie-player animation component. Websites loading unpinned <script src="https://unpkg.com/@lottiefiles/lottie-player@latest"> tags automatically serve a trojanized bundle that opens a WebSocket C2 to wss://castleservices.org and overlays an AceDrainer crypto phishing modal. Across this 3-step forensic reconstruction, incident responders correlate primary host, kernel, identity, and network telemetry (capturing exact Event IDs, syscall numbers, registry/filesystem structures, and protocol fields so defenders can verify root cause and scope compromise with high confidence).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Compromised NPM Token Pushes `@lottiefiles/lottie-player` v2.0.5, v2.0.6 & v2.0.7 (T1195.002) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Obfuscated Bundle Execution & WebSocket C2 Handshake (`wss://castleservices.org`) (T1059.007) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection & AceDrainer `eth_sendTransaction` / `Permit2` Signing (T1185)
- **Primary Sources:** [LottieFiles Official Security Incident Report: Incident Report: @lottiefiles/lottie-player npm Package Versions 2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7 Unauthorized Release (Oct 2024)](https://lottiefiles.com/blog/working-with-lottie/incident-report-unauthorized-access-to-lottie-player-npm-package); [Scam Sniffer, Blockaid & Phylum Supply-Chain Research: Dissecting the @lottiefiles/lottie-player CDN Supply-Chain Attack: WebSocket C2 wss://castleservices.org & WalletConnect Modal Injection](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/); [The MITRE Corporation: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.002 (Supply Chain Compromise) & T1189 (Drive-by Compromise via Unpinned unpkg/jsDelivr CDN)](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/)

### T1539: CircleCI Official Security Alert, GitHub Security & CISA — CircleCI CI/CD Supply Chain Breach: Engineer macOS Infostealer, 2FA Session Theft & Customer Vault Exfiltration
- **ID:** `circleci-oauth-github-token-rotation-breach`

- **Category:** SUPPLY_CHAIN_CICD | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a high-security facility where an intruder attempts to operate covertly across Threat Actor (Stolen macOS SSO Session Cookie), Engineer macOS Laptop (Infostealer Malware), and CircleCI Production Bastion & KMS Key Service, unaware that every system call, protocol handshake, and on-disk structural table (Customer CI/CD Secrets, SSH Keys & GitHub Tokens) automatically records an immutable forensic ledger entry correlated by CircleCI / GitHub OAuth & AWS CloudTrail Sensor. Grounded in the official CircleCI Incident Report (January 2023), GitHub Security Advisories, and CISA CI/CD Supply Chain Guidance: an attacker compromises a CircleCI site reliability engineer’s macOS laptop with infostealer malware, steals an active 2FA-authenticated SSO session cookie from browser storage, impersonates the engineer in production, and extracts customer environment variables, AWS IAM keys, and GitHub OAuth deployment tokens. Across this 3-step forensic reconstruction, incident responders correlate primary host, kernel, identity, and network telemetry (capturing exact Event IDs, syscall numbers, registry/filesystem structures, and protocol fields so defenders can verify root cause and scope compromise with high confidence).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Engineer macOS Infostealer Infection & 2FA-Backed Browser Session Cookie Theft (T1539) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: Session Replay from Foreign IP, Production Database Access & KMS Key Extraction (T1550.004) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Offline Decryption of Customer CI/CD Secrets & Downstream GitHub / AWS Token Replay (T1552.001)
- **Primary Sources:** [CircleCI Official Security Incident Report: CircleCI January 4, 2023 Security Incident Report: Engineer Laptop Malware, 2FA SSO Session Theft & Customer Secret Rotation](https://circleci.com/blog/jan-4-2023-incident-report/); [GitHub Security & CISA Supply Chain Guidance: Auditing GitHub Enterprise OAuth Apps, Deploy Keys, and CI/CD Pipeline Secret Access After Provider Compromise](https://www.cisa.gov/resources-tools/resources/defending-continuous-integrationcontinuous-delivery-cicd-environments); [The MITRE Corporation: MITRE ATT&CK T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie), T1552.001 & T1550.001 (Application Access Token)](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/)

### T1190: Rapid7, JetBrains & CISA AA24-249A — JetBrains TeamCity Auth Bypass (CVE-2024-27198) to CI/CD Build Pipeline Poisoning & Signed Release Tampering
- **ID:** `jetbrains-teamcity-cve-2024-27198-supply-chain-build-poisoning`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/jetbrains-teamcity-cve-2024-27198-supply-chain-build-poisoning
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=jetbrains-teamcity-cve-2024-27198-supply-chain-build-poisoning
- **Category:** SUPPLY_CHAIN_CICD | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a high-security facility where an intruder attempts to operate covertly across Threat Actor (CVE-2024-27198 Exploit), JetBrains TeamCity Server (:8111 ;.jsp Bypass), and TeamCity REST API (Admin Token & Build Step Injection), unaware that every system call, protocol handshake, and on-disk structural table (Signed Enterprise Build Artifacts & Downstream Hosts) automatically records an immutable forensic ledger entry correlated by Rapid7 / CISA TeamCity Audit & EDR Sensor. Grounded in Rapid7 Vulnerability Research, JetBrains Security Advisory, and CISA Advisories on CVE-2024-27198 (CVSS 9.8): attackers exploit an unauthenticated URL path-handling flaw (/hax?jsp=/app/rest/users;.jsp) in JetBrains TeamCity CI/CD servers to mint an administrator access token (POST /app/rest/users/id:1/tokens/RPC2), inject malicious build steps into enterprise software release pipelines, and sign trojanized build artifacts. Across this 3-step forensic reconstruction, incident responders correlate primary host, kernel, identity, and network telemetry (capturing exact Event IDs, syscall numbers, registry/filesystem structures, and protocol fields so defenders can verify root cause and scope compromise with high confidence).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Unauthenticated `;.jsp` Matrix Parameter Auth Bypass (CVE-2024-27198) & Admin Token Minting (T1190) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: CI/CD Build Step Injection (`/app/rest/buildTypes`) & Signing Key Access (T1195.002) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: Trojanized Build Compilation, Official Code Signing & Downstream Distribution (T1195.002)
- **Primary Sources:** [Rapid7 Emergent Threat Response & JetBrains Security: CVE-2024-27198 & CVE-2024-27199: JetBrains TeamCity Authentication Bypass & RCE Technical Analysis](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/2024/03/04/etr-cve-2024-27198-and-cve-2024-27199-jetbrains-teamcity-multiple-authentication-bypass-vulnerabilities-fixed/); [CISA, FBI, NSA & NCSC-UK Joint Advisory: AA24-249A: Russian Military Cyber Actors (APT29 / Cozy Bear) Target U.S. and Global Infrastructure via TeamCity CVE-2024-27198](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa24-249a); [Microsoft Threat Intelligence & The MITRE Corporation: Octo Tempest, BianLian & Midnight Blizzard Exploitation of TeamCity CI/CD Servers — MITRE T1190 / T1195.002](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/)

### T1195.001: PyTorch Official Security Advisory, Sonatype & MITRE T1195.001 — PyTorch torchtriton Nightly Dependency Confusion Supply Chain Attack & h4ck.cfd DNS Exfiltration
- **ID:** `pypi-pytorch-torchtriton-dependency-confusion-supply-chain`
- **Canonical URL:** https://attackexplorer.org/scenarios/pypi-pytorch-torchtriton-dependency-confusion-supply-chain
- **Simulator Deep Link:** https://attackexplorer.org/?scenario=pypi-pytorch-torchtriton-dependency-confusion-supply-chain
- **Category:** SUPPLY_CHAIN_CICD | **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **Overview:** Imagine a high-security facility where an intruder attempts to operate covertly across Attacker Authoritative DNS (*.h4ck.cfd), Public PyPI Registry (Namespace-Squatted torchtriton), and AI/ML Workstation & GPU Cluster (pip --extra-index-url), unaware that every system call, protocol handshake, and on-disk structural table (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials & .gitconfig Exfiltrated) automatically records an immutable forensic ledger entry correlated by Linux Auditd & Passive DNS Entropy Sensor. Grounded in the official PyTorch Security Advisory, Sonatype, and Wiz Research on the torchtriton dependency confusion attack: because pip install --extra-index-url does not give precedence to private/nightly registries over the public PyPI index, registering a higher-versioned torchtriton package on public PyPI caused pip to install a trojanized wheel containing an ELF binary (triton/runtime/triton) that exfiltrated SSH keys, AWS credentials, and /etc/passwd over encrypted DNS queries to *.h4ck.cfd. Across this 3-step forensic reconstruction, incident responders correlate primary host, kernel, identity, and network telemetry (capturing exact Event IDs, syscall numbers, registry/filesystem structures, and protocol fields so defenders can verify root cause and scope compromise with high confidence).
- **Stages (3):** Stage 1: Stage 1: Public PyPI Namespace Squatting & `pip --extra-index-url` Precedence Hijack (T1195.001) -> Stage 2: Stage 2: `__init__.py` Execution of Compiled ELF Stealer (`triton/runtime/triton`) (T1059.006) -> Stage 3: Stage 3: AES-Encrypted DNS Tunneling Exfiltration via `wheezy.io` to `*.h4ck.cfd` (T1048.003)
- **Primary Sources:** [PyTorch Foundation Official Security Advisory: Compromised PyTorch-Nightly Dependency Chain Between Dec 25 and Dec 30, 2022 (torchtriton on PyPI)](https://pytorch.org/blog/compromised-nightly-dependency/); [CISA & NSA Software Supply Chain Guidance: Mitigating Dependency Confusion (Namespace Shadowing) Across Public PyPI and Private Package Indexes](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/001/); [The MITRE Corporation & MITRE ATLAS™: MITRE ATT&CK T1195.001 (Compromise Software Dependencies) & T1048.003 (DNS Exfiltration via *.h4ck.cfd)](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/001/)
